title: REPORT on discharge in respect of the implementation of the general budget of the European Union for the financial year 2024, Section I – European Parliament
part_text: 19. Recalls that, in accordance with Articles 1.3.2, 2.7.1 and 2.7.2 of the Rules on the use of appropriations from budget item 400, the former political group Identity & Democracy (ID Group) submitted its final financial report on 8 October 2024 covering the period from 1 January to 15 July 2024; recalls that Parliament’s administration received the ID Group’s full financial archive in both electronic and paper format and conducted a risk-based ex-post verification of the 2024 accounts, focusing on consistency checks and sample testing of high-risk contracts and donations; recalls the findings of Parliament’s administration that at least EUR 4 333 635,78 of budget item 400 appropriations were unduly spent by the group over the 2019-2024 term, exposing Parliament to a significant financial and reputational risk; shortcomings in the public procurement procedures were identified, and represent significant reputational risks for Parliament; questions, in light of the Committee on Budgetary Control’s opinion on the 2024 accounts of the Identity and Democracy Group, the criteria for selecting external auditors for DGFINS; emphasises that the CONT opinion concerning the ID Group was discussed by the Bureau of the European Parliament on November 24, 2025, in camera, and that the minutes of that meeting do not reflect any decision on the various points raised; recalls that the Bureau does not represent all political groups; recalls that the accounts in question had received an unqualified opinion from the external auditor; consequently asks DG FINS to clarify the criteria used to select external auditors to date and to disclose the number of checks it has carried out to ensure that external auditors provide work that meets the highest standards of rigor and professionalism; finally, in the interest of equal treatment, calls on the Bureau to commission an audit of all political groups whose accounts have been certified by the same external auditor for at least the past six years; calls on the Bureau to make public, in real time, all expenditures of the political groups, as well as the contracts and public procurement procedures of the various groups;
